title: AuthorizationResponseEnvelope
description: W3C VerifiablePresentation envelope carrying issuer-signed credentials about the beneficiary PSP (counterparty), sent alongside a signed AuthorizationResponse on the authorization-response path, from the beneficiary PSP through the counterparty gateway to the payment gateway. Response-side mirror of PaymentRequestEnvelope (the request side): the holder MUST be the same did:pkh that signed the inner AuthorizationResponse — the verifier asserts equality after independently verifying both proofs. The VP envelope design applied to the counterparty authorization response.

version.description: Semver-shaped declaration version (MAJOR.MINOR). The major component is locked to this schema's parent directory (v1 → major must be 1). Producers MUST emit the canonical value exported by the bindings' Version constant; the canonical bumps on each additive minor evolution.

@context.description: JSON-LD context array. MUST include BOTH the W3C VC v1 context (https://www.w3.org/2018/credentials/v1) and the AuthorizationResponseEnvelope v1 context (https://schemas.atum.network/declarations/AuthorizationResponseEnvelope/v1/context.jsonld) — without the envelope context, JSON-LD expansion drops envelope-specific terms (challenge, domain, holder) during URDNA2015 canonicalization, so the replay-binding fields end up outside the signed n-quad graph.

type.description: MUST contain 'VerifiablePresentation' per W3C VC Data Model v1.1.

holder.description: did:pkh URI of the beneficiary PSP (counterparty) presenting the credentials. The verifier asserts holder equals the recovered signer of the inner AuthorizationResponse — they MUST match. did:pkh form is mandated to keep the holder anchored to a chain account that can be cryptographically recovered from the signature, mirroring the originator-side shape used by PaymentRequestEnvelope.

verifiableCredential.description: Array of issuer-signed credentials about the beneficiary PSP. One VC per concern (psp-role / jurisdiction / etc.), all riding in this array. The verifier's policy decides which types are required and which issuers are trusted. MVP requires at least one VC in the array; future ticket can relax to allow zero (a bare VP with just a holder proof) if a use case emerges. maxItems matches ld-verification's defaultMaxVerifiableCredentials — an unauthenticated DoS backstop at the schema layer mirroring the verifier's default.

proof.description: Holder-signed W3C Data Integrity proof. proofPurpose MUST be 'authentication'; challenge MUST equal the authorization response hash — the content-addressed hash of the inner AuthorizationResponse this envelope wraps ("0x"+keccak256 over the canonicalized, proof-stripped AuthorizationResponse), recomputed by the verifier from the inner response it receives. This mirrors the request-side PaymentRequestEnvelope, which binds challenge to its OWN inner declaration's hash (the PaymentRequest's request_hash); the response side uses the AuthorizationResponse's own content hash, NOT the PaymentRequest's request_hash (request_hash is the request's identity, not the response's). domain MUST equal the verifier's configured service identifier, the NETWORK-WIDE value `did:web:<env>.atum.network` (same shape as PaymentRequestEnvelope, distinct from FQE's `did:web:settler.<env>.atum.network`).

VPDataIntegrityProof.description: W3C Data Integrity proof for a VerifiablePresentation. Extends the base DataIntegrityProof with challenge and domain per W3C VC Data Model 5.6. proofPurpose is constrained to 'authentication': the holder is authenticating themselves as the presenter of the enclosed credentials.

type.description: Proof type identifier. MUST be one of EcdsaSecp256k1RecoverySignature2020 (secp256k1) or Ed25519Signature2020 (ed25519), and MUST equal the inner declaration's proof.type so the holder-binding consistency check anchors both signatures to the same cryptosuite.

created.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the proof was created. Canonicalize the value exactly as it appears in the raw JSON: parsing it into a date-time and re-serializing can change the spelling (Z versus +00:00), and a different spelling canonicalizes to different bytes, so the signature no longer verifies. The verifier also checks freshness against its configured maximum proof age and future-skew window.

verificationMethod.description: DID URL identifying the verification method, e.g., 'did:pkh:eip155:1:0x...#blockchainAccountId' for ECDSA or 'did:pkh:solana:<chain>:<addr>#SolanaMethod2021' for Ed25519 on Solana, or 'did:pkh:stellar:<network>:<G-account>#blockchainAccountId' for Ed25519 on Stellar. The recovered identity from this MUST match the holder field.

proofPurpose.description: Always 'authentication' for VerifiablePresentation proofs per W3C VC Data Model §5.6 — the holder is authenticating themselves as the presenter of the enclosed credentials.

challenge.description: Replay-binding challenge. The verifier requires this to equal the authorization response hash — the content-addressed hash of the inner AuthorizationResponse this envelope wraps, formatted "0x"+64-lowercase-hex (keccak256 over the canonicalized, proof-stripped AuthorizationResponse). The verifier recomputes it from the inner AuthorizationResponse it receives and asserts equality, binding the holder's VP (and its VCs) to exactly this response so the envelope can't be lifted onto a different one. This mirrors PaymentRequestEnvelope, which binds challenge to its OWN inner declaration's content hash (the PaymentRequest's request_hash); the response side uses the AuthorizationResponse's own content hash, NOT the PaymentRequest's request_hash (the request's identity, not the response's) and NOT payment_id (a mutable correlator). Replay across payments is prevented because payment_id is part of the AuthorizationResponse's canonical content, so distinct payments yield distinct response hashes.

domain.description: Replay-binding domain. The verifier requires this to equal its configured service identifier — locked to a NETWORK-WIDE value `did:web:<env>.atum.network` (e.g., `did:web:atum.network`). Distinct from FQE's `did:web:settler.<env>.atum.network` so a captured envelope can't be misrouted to FQE-shaped verifiers. Without this, a captured envelope from one environment could be replayed against another by the same holder.

jws.description: Detached JWS signature in <base64url(header)>..<base64url(sig)> form, header {alg:ES256K-R, b64:false, crit:[b64]}. Used by the EcdsaSecp256k1RecoverySignature2020 cryptosuite. Exactly one of jws / proofValue must be present, matching the cryptosuite.

proofValue.description: Multibase z-base58btc-encoded 64-byte signature. Used by the Ed25519Signature2020 cryptosuite. Exactly one of jws / proofValue must be present, matching the cryptosuite.

VerifiableCredential.description: W3C Verifiable Credential structure conforming to the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model v1.1

issuer.description: DID or issuer object of the credential issuer

credentialSubject.description: Claims about the credential subject (structure varies by issuer)

credentialStatus.description: Information for credential revocation checking. Not consulted by the verifier today.
